name: Risograph
summary: A digital stencil duplicator: a thermal head cuts a master, and a drum pushes soy ink through it in one spot colour.
how: Separate the design into 1–4 spot colours and give each layer as a greyscale file.
Print one drum (one colour) at a pass and feed the sheets again for the next colour.
Keep tones on a grain or halftone screen of 50–110 lines an inch; avoid large solids.
Use uncoated paper, and let the ink dry before a second pass to stop set-off.

origin.note: Riso Kagaku sells the first machine under the Risograph name, for schools, churches and offices.

adoptions.via: Art and zine studios buy used duplicators and print books and posters in fluorescent spot inks.
